href="#%e8%bf%9e%e6%8e%a5%e4%b8%a4%e4%b8%aa%e7%95%8c%e9%9d%a2" title="连接两个界面">连接两个界面</a> <a href="#%e8%bf%9e%e6%8e%a5%e4%b8%a4%e4%b8%aa%e7%95%8c%e9%9d%a2" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="连接两个界面">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>/ide </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>在交互式 Copilot CLI 会话中使用 <code>/ide</code></strong>，检查或修改 VS Code 连接。 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="连接指南"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/connecting-vs-code"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/use-copilot-cli/connecting-vs-code" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >连接指南</a> </span> 说明可信工作区匹配、编辑器选择共享，以及将拟议文件编辑显示为差异。</p> <p><strong>自动连接取决于工作区匹配。</strong> 本地 CLI 不会仅因仓库名称相同就连接远程 Codespace。要在对应环境运行 CLI。宽泛的编辑授权也会绕过拟议编辑的差异批准流程。预期提示消失时检查权限。</p> <p><strong>CLI 转录内容会出现在 VS Code 的 Sessions 视图中</strong>，并可通过 Resume in Terminal 继续。这保留了终端工作流，但不要认为对话已变成可互换的原生编辑器代理会话。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>连接前</th> <th>核实</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>工作区</strong></td> <td>目标文件夹已打开并受信任</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>执行位置</strong></td> <td>CLI 和编辑器集成指向同一环境</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>选择区域</strong></td> <td>高亮代码符合当前请求</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>权限</strong></td> <td>需要时拟议编辑审查仍保持启用</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>会话</strong></td> <td>正在继续目标对话</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="模型计费和策略"> <a href="#%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e8%ae%a1%e8%b4%b9%e5%92%8c%e7%ad%96%e7%95%a5" title="模型、计费和策略">模型、计费和策略</a> <a href="#%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e8%ae%a1%e8%b4%b9%e5%92%8c%e7%ad%96%e7%95%a5" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="模型、计费和策略">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>在可用时用同一选定模型测试两个界面。</strong> 如果模型选项不同，记录差异。模型、上下文选择或工具集不同，会让试验超出图形与终端的区别。</p> <p><strong>核实账户中的当前用量计算。</strong> GitHub 的 Agent 模式文档提到 AI Credits。不要在未检查当前计费安排前套用旧的高级请求估算。CLI 提示和编辑器任务不自动等价于相同工作量。</p> <p><strong>组织访问是前提。</strong> 缺少功能时，先检查策略，再重新安装扩展。记录两种界面获准的工具和集成。提供商登录不会自动授权修改每个仓库或联系每个外部服务。</p> <h2 id="执行配对试验"> <a href="#%e6%89%a7%e8%a1%8c%e9%85%8d%e5%af%b9%e8%af%95%e9%aa%8c" title="执行配对试验">执行配对试验</a> <a href="#%e6%89%a7%e8%a1%8c%e9%85%8d%e5%af%b9%e8%af%95%e9%aa%8c" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="执行配对试验">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>准备同一初始修订的两份副本。</strong> 使用匹配的说明和验收测试。第一次在独立 CLI 中执行，第二次在 VS Code Agent 模式中执行。只有混合交互符合日常工作时，才增加连接 CLI 的第三次试验。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>测量项</th> <th>记录原因</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>提供的上下文</strong></td> <td>揭示隐藏的手动准备工作</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>正确性</strong></td> <td>区分看似合理的代码和已验证修复</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>批准步骤</strong></td> <td>显示相同策略下的监督负担</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>审查时间</strong></td> <td>衡量理解完整补丁的时间</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>手动修复</strong></td> <td>记录代理完成后的剩余工作</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>用量</strong></td> <td>将成本与接受的结果关联</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>把恢复过程保留在测试中。</strong> 拒绝一个拟议方案并说明原因。观察下一次尝试是否保留有用工作并遵守修正。这比一次不间断演示更能反映日常使用。</p> <h2 id="故障排查和下一步"> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e6%9f%a5%e5%92%8c%e4%b8%8b%e4%b8%80%e6%ad%a5" title="故障排查和下一步">故障排查和下一步</a> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e6%9f%a5%e5%92%8c%e4%b8%8b%e4%b8%80%e6%ad%a5" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="故障排查和下一步">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>如果 CLI 连接到错误的编辑器窗口</strong>，检查 <code>/ide</code> 并选择目标工作区。如果可视化批准停止出现，检查宽泛编辑权限。如果 Agent 模式不可用，检查扩展状态和组织策略。</p> <p><strong>选择独立 CLI</strong>，当 shell 上下文和可重复调用占主导。<strong>选择 VS Code</strong>，当基于选择的上下文、内联工作和图形审查占主导。<strong>使用连接 CLI</strong>，当终端任务输入和编辑器检查配合良好。</p> <p><strong>进行跨供应商比较时</strong>，阅读 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI 主比较"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI 主比较</a> </span> 或 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="GUI 主比较"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/gui-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >GUI 主比较</a> </span> 。将这些评估与本次同系列界面试验分开。</p> Read More at https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: GUI 编程代理比较：Cursor、Windsurf、Cline、Copilot 与 Continue
item.category: "开发者工具" , "人工智能" , "软件开发"
item.description: 比较图形化编程代理，区分完整编辑器与扩展，并检查 Roo Code 停止服务的背景、模型访问、批准和审查流程。
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>图形化编程代理</strong>把任务对话放在文件、差异、诊断和应用预览旁边。本指南比较 Cursor、Windsurf/Cascade 产品线、VS Code 的 Cline 扩展、VS Code 中的 GitHub Copilot，以及 Continue IDE 扩展。Roo Code 被列为旧迁移选项，因为其文档已经报告停止服务。</p> <p>**先选择工作区，再选择模型。**独立编辑器会改变开发环境。扩展会把代理加入现有编辑器。请同时评估生成的补丁和检查补丁所需的工作量。</p> <h2 id="要点"> <a href="#%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" title="要点">要点</a> <a href="#%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="要点">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Cursor 和 Windsurf 产品线</strong>属于完整编辑器。</li> <li><strong>Cline、Copilot 和 Continue</strong>在现有编辑器中提供代理流程。</li> <li><strong>Roo Code 需要迁移计划</strong>，不应当作普通的新部署。</li> <li><strong>可见的修改仍需要测试</strong>、依赖审查和明确的接受决定。</li> </ul> <p>**范围和日期：**官方文档于 2026 年 10 月 6 日检查。这是流程比较，不是速度或代码质量基准。终端产品另见 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI 比较"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/"> <a href="/articles/cli-coding-agents-comparison/" rel="follow me" >CLI 比较</a> </span> 。</p> <p>**前提：**已有项目、可运行的测试，以及安装所选编辑器或扩展的权限。难度为初级到中级。为两个产品试用安排一个下午。</p> <h2 id="当前名称和状态"> <a href="#%e5%bd%93%e5%89%8d%e5%90%8d%e7%a7%b0%e5%92%8c%e7%8a%b6%e6%80%81" title="当前名称和状态">当前名称和状态</a> <a href="#%e5%bd%93%e5%89%8d%e5%90%8d%e7%a7%b0%e5%92%8c%e7%8a%b6%e6%80%81" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="当前名称和状态">#</a> </h2> <p>**Windsurf 的 Cascade 文档会重定向到 Devin Desktop。**当前的 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Cascade 参考"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade"> <a href="https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/cascade/cascade" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Cascade 参考</a> </span> 把 Cascade 放在 Devin Desktop 中，旁边还有另一个本地代理。本文使用“Windsurf/Cascade”连接熟悉的名称与当前文档。重现旧教程前，请检查已安装的产品和选定的代理。</p> <p><strong>Roo Code 文档报告扩展将于 2026-05-15 停止。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="官方通知"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/"> <a href="https://roocodeinc.github.io/Roo-Code/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >官方通知</a> </span> 指向替代方案。现有代码或归档说明不代表仍在维护。除非另行评估受维护的 fork、所有权、发布和支持，否则不要在新部署中使用 Roo。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>产品界面</th> <th>类别</th> <th>在候选列表中的作用</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Cursor 编辑器</strong></td> <td>完整图形编辑器</td> <td>集成代理和审查流程</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Windsurf/Cascade</strong></td> <td>完整图形编辑器系列</td> <td>Devin Desktop 中的当前 Cascade 流程</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>VS Code 中的 Cline</strong></td> <td>编辑器扩展</td> <td>提供商选择和工具任务</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>VS Code 中的 Copilot</strong></td> <td>编辑器集成</td> <td>建议、聊天和代理工作</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Continue 扩展</strong></td> <td>编辑器扩展</td> <td>可配置模型和任务模式</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Roo Code</strong></td> <td>旧扩展</td> <td>迁移参考，不是当前推荐</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="完整编辑器"> <a href="#%e5%ae%8c%e6%95%b4%e7%bc%96%e8%be%91%e5%99%a8" title="完整编辑器">完整编辑器</a> <a href="#%e5%ae%8c%e6%95%b4%e7%bc%96%e8%be%91%e5%99%a8" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="完整编辑器">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Cursor Agent</strong>组合指令、工具和所选模型。 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="代理概览"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview"> <a href="https://cursor.com/docs/agent/overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >代理概览</a> </span> 记录文件修改、终端执行、浏览器交互和检查点。检查点独立于 Git，可用于会话恢复，而提交应作为持久的审查记录。</p> <p><strong>Cascade</strong>提供代码和聊天模式、编辑器上下文、工具和检查点。当前文档说明会自动加入选定的编辑器或终端文本。评估时记录提供的上下文和活动代理。更换周围编辑器或本地代理会改变比较结果。</p> <p>**完整编辑器试用需要迁移检查。**在测量代理输出前，检查现有工作区的语言支持、格式化、调试、快捷键和扩展。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>编辑器测试</th> <th>应收集的证据</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>项目启动</strong></td> <td>现有构建和启动任务仍然可用</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>语言工具</strong></td> <td>诊断和导航符合基线</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>代理修改</strong></td> <td>修改出现在可审查的差异中</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>恢复</strong></td> <td>撤销保留无关的手动工作</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>应用检查</strong></td> <td>测试和交互行为一致</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="编辑器中的扩展"> <a href="#%e7%bc%96%e8%be%91%e5%99%a8%e4%b8%ad%e7%9a%84%e6%89%a9%e5%b1%95" title="编辑器中的扩展">编辑器中的扩展</a> <a href="#%e7%bc%96%e8%be%91%e5%99%a8%e4%b8%ad%e7%9a%84%e6%89%a9%e5%b1%95" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="编辑器中的扩展">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>VS Code 的 Cline 扩展</strong>读取和写入文件、执行命令并使用编辑器工具。 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="概览"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.cline.bot/cline-overview"> <a href="https://docs.cline.bot/cline-overview" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >概览</a> </span> 说明包括提供商凭据和本地运行时在内的模型访问方式。<strong>VS Code 中的 GitHub Copilot</strong>提供建议、聊天和代理修改。 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="IDE 概览"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides"> <a href="https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/copilot-surfaces/copilot-in-ides" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >IDE 概览</a> </span> 区分这些体验。<strong>Continue 扩展</strong>区分 Chat、Plan 和 Agent。 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Agent 快速开始"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://docs.continue.dev/ide-extensions/agent/quick-start"> <a href="https://docs.continue.dev/ide-extensions/agent/quick-start" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Agent 快速开始</a> </span> 说明只读规划和工具实现。连接了模型并不能证明代理配置可用。</p> <p>扩展减少编辑器迁移工作，但配置仍然重要。检查冲突快捷键、语言服务器、工具批准和所选提供商。首次试用时停用竞争的代理扩展。</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/editor-extension-review-workflow.webp", "caption": "完整编辑器和扩展布局汇聚到可视化差异、诊断面板和独立测试清单", "license": "https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/", "acquireLicensePage": "https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/", "creditText": "SimeonOnSecurity", "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:17:13.925118121 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b143.865264744", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:17:13.925118121 +0000 UTC m=+143.865264744"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/editor-extension-review-workflow.webp" alt="完整编辑器和扩展布局汇聚到可视化差异、诊断面板和独立测试清单"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>比较检查和接受修改所需的工作量</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="审查和控制"> <a href="#%e5%ae%a1%e6%9f%a5%e5%92%8c%e6%8e%a7%e5%88%b6" title="审查和控制">审查和控制</a> <a href="#%e5%ae%a1%e6%9f%a5%e5%92%8c%e6%8e%a7%e5%88%b6" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="审查和控制">#</a> </h2> <p>**有用的 GUI 会显示决策依据。**查找修改的文件、命令输出、待处理操作以及重新引导工作的清晰方式。**分开批准和最终接受。**允许命令只代表代理可以执行工作。接受最终补丁代表你已经检查范围和行为。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>审查问题</th> <th>检查内容</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>改了什么？</strong></td> <td>完整差异，包括配置和锁文件</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>为什么改？</strong></td> <td>需求与每次编辑的联系</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>运行了什么？</strong></td> <td>命令、退出状态和有用输出</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>什么失败？</strong></td> <td>未解决错误和放弃的方法</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>什么可恢复？</strong></td> <td>检查点行为和 Git 基线</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>在一次性项目副本中，用已有的未提交编辑测试恢复。让代理做独立修改，撤销该修改，确认原编辑仍然存在。</p> <h2 id="模型隐私和计费"> <a href="#%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e9%9a%90%e7%a7%81%e5%92%8c%e8%ae%a1%e8%b4%b9" title="模型、隐私和计费">模型、隐私和计费</a> <a href="#%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e9%9a%90%e7%a7%81%e5%92%8c%e8%ae%a1%e8%b4%b9" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="模型、隐私和计费">#</a> </h2> <p>**编辑器窗口不会说明推理目的地。**记录模型、提供商账户、仓库索引行为、工具连接和执行环境。本地扩展与本地模型是不同属性。**价格要绑定访问方式。**订阅额度、托管服务使用和提供商 API 计费是不同安排。团队部署还要检查批准模型、安装更新政策、凭据、仓库排除项和支持责任。</p> <h2 id="实用候选列表"> <a href="#%e5%ae%9e%e7%94%a8%e5%80%99%e9%80%89%e5%88%97%e8%a1%a8" title="实用候选列表">实用候选列表</a> <a href="#%e5%ae%9e%e7%94%a8%e5%80%99%e9%80%89%e5%88%97%e8%a1%a8" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="实用候选列表">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>起始情况</th> <th>首先比较</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>愿意更换编辑器</strong></td> <td>Cursor 与当前 Windsurf/Cascade</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>保留 VS Code 和 Copilot</strong></td> <td>Copilot Agent 模式与 Cline</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>自行选择提供商</strong></td> <td>Cline 与 Continue</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>从 Roo Code 迁移</strong></td> <td>Cline 与另一项当前受维护的选择</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>主要手写代码</strong></td> <td>先用行内辅助，再用委派任务</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>选择一个失败函数，请求诊断，批准有限修复，检查差异并运行独立测试。保持对话打开并手动修改，观察下一轮代理是否保留修改。记录任务正确性、手动提供的上下文、批准中断、审查工作和恢复行为。</p> <h2 id="故障排除和下一步"> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e9%99%a4%e5%92%8c%e4%b8%8b%e4%b8%80%e6%ad%a5" title="故障排除和下一步">故障排除和下一步</a> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e9%99%a4%e5%92%8c%e4%b8%8b%e4%b8%80%e6%ad%a5" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="故障排除和下一步">#</a> </h2> <p>**禁用的代理模式通常需要检查设置。**确认模型工具支持、工作区信任、组织策略和扩展兼容性。如果编辑器诊断与命令行测试不一致，请检查解释器选择和环境变量。</p> <p>初次试用后选择一个编辑器配置使用一周，并记录接受的修改和修复。使用 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Copilot CLI 与 VS Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/"> <a href="/articles/github-copilot-cli-vs-vscode/" rel="follow me" >Copilot CLI 与 VS Code</a> </span> ，或在各自产品系列中比较 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Codex"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/codex-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Codex</a> </span> 、 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Claude Code"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/claude-code-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >Claude Code</a> </span> 和 <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode"> <meta itemprop="url" content="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/"> <a href="/articles/opencode-cli-vs-desktop/" rel="follow me" >OpenCode</a> </span> 。</p> Read More at https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: OpenCode CLI 对比 Desktop：2026 工作流比较
item.category: "开发者工具" , "人工智能" , "软件开发"
item.description: 从服务器架构、提供商配置、脚本、会话状态和故障排除方面比较 OpenCode 的终端客户端与桌面客户端。
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>OpenCode CLI 和 Desktop 是同一个编码代理产品的客户端。</strong> 终端界面适合键盘驱动的工作和脚本。桌面应用提供图形化工作区。重要的比较包括每个客户端背后的服务器、项目、提供商和配置。</p> <p><strong>先确认后端，再选择界面。</strong> 两个 OpenCode 窗口不一定使用同一个服务器或会话。连接到不同服务器的桌面应用属于不同的执行环境，即使模型标签看起来熟悉。</p> <h2 id="核心要点"> <a href="#%e6%a0%b8%e5%bf%83%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" title="核心要点">核心要点</a> <a href="#%e6%a0%b8%e5%bf%83%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="核心要点">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>终端工作和非交互命令使用 CLI。</strong></li> <li><strong>图形化工作区使用 Desktop</strong>，同时检查所选服务器。</li> <li><strong>提供商配置决定推理过程</strong>，与界面无关。</li> <li><strong>相同的产品身份不保证不同服务器或版本之间共享会话状态。</strong></li> </ul> <p><strong>范围和日期：</strong> 官方文档于 2026 年 10 月 6 日检查。本指南比较界面，不比较模型质量。你需要一个仓库、正常工作的提供商连接和基本终端知识。为试用预留 45 至 60 分钟。</p> <h2 id="客户端与服务器"> <a href="#%e5%ae%a2%e6%88%b7%e7%ab%af%e4%b8%8e%e6%9c%8d%e5%8a%a1%e5%99%a8" title="客户端与服务器">客户端与服务器</a> <a href="#%e5%ae%a2%e6%88%b7%e7%ab%af%e4%b8%8e%e6%9c%8d%e5%8a%a1%e5%99%a8" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="客户端与服务器">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode 将界面与服务器分开。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="服务器文档"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/server/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/server/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >服务器文档</a> </span> 将终端 UI 描述为客户端，将 <code>opencode serve</code> 描述为独立服务器。这种架构支持多种与代理交互的方式。</p> <p><strong>Desktop 默认启动本地服务器。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="故障排除指南"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/troubleshooting/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >故障排除指南</a> </span> 介绍其 <code>opencode-cli</code> sidecar，以及连接到已配置服务器 URL 的选项。当客户端行为不同时，先检查此连接，再修改提示词。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>层</th> <th>要回答的问题</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>客户端</strong></td> <td>终端 UI、桌面应用还是非交互命令？</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>代理服务器</strong></td> <td>哪个进程接收请求？</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>仓库</strong></td> <td>服务器访问哪个目录？</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>模型提供商</strong></td> <td>哪个服务提供推理？</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>会话</strong></td> <td>已有对话还是新任务？</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>服务器位置不等于推理位置。</strong> 运行在你电脑上的代理服务器仍会把请求发送到已配置的托管模型。相反，兼容的本地推理服务是独立进程，拥有自己的模型和资源要求。</p> <p>官方服务器参考将 <code>127.0.0.1</code> 列为 <code>opencode serve</code> 的默认主机名。本地试用时，将服务保持在 loopback：</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>opencode serve --hostname 127.0.0.1 </span></span></code></pre></div><p>只有在确定身份验证、防火墙规则以及服务器可访问的仓库路径后，才使用更宽的绑定地址。</p> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org/", "@type": "ImageObject", "contentUrl": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/opencode-clients-server-provider.webp", "caption": "creator": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity" }, "copyrightNotice": "SimeonOnSecurity", "associatedArticle": { "@type": "NewsArticle", "headline": "simeononsecurity", "url": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/", "datePublished": "2026-10-22 04:17:13.928729084 \u002b0000 UTC m=\u002b143.868875706", "author": { "@type": "Person", "name": "SimeonOnSecurity", "url": "https:\/\/zh.simeononsecurity.com\/authors\/simeononsecurity" } } } </script> <center> <figure align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/ImageObject"> <meta property="article:published_time" content="2026-10-22 04:17:13.928729084 +0000 UTC m=+143.868875706"> <meta property="article:author" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <meta property="article:author:url" content="https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/authors/simeononsecurity"> <meta property="og:license" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/termsandconditions/"> <meta property="og:see_also" content="https://simeononsecurity.com/contactus/"> <meta property="og:copyright" content="SimeonOnSecurity"> <img align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 80%; max-height: 600px; min-width: 100px; min-height: 100px; height: auto; width: auto;" src="https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/opencode-clients-server-provider.webp" alt="连接到代理服务器、仓库文件和独立推理服务的终端与桌面客户端"loading="lazy" fetchpriority="low" itemprop="contentUrl" /> <figcaption align="center" style="text-align: center; margin: 0 auto;" itemprop="caption description"> <p>分别检查代理服务器和推理提供商</p> </figcaption> </figure> </center> <h2 id="终端交互与自动化"> <a href="#%e7%bb%88%e7%ab%af%e4%ba%a4%e4%ba%92%e4%b8%8e%e8%87%aa%e5%8a%a8%e5%8c%96" title="终端交互与自动化">终端交互与自动化</a> <a href="#%e7%bb%88%e7%ab%af%e4%ba%a4%e4%ba%92%e4%b8%8e%e8%87%aa%e5%8a%a8%e5%8c%96" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="终端交互与自动化">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>opencode </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>默认命令会打开终端 UI。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="CLI 参考"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/cli/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >CLI 参考</a> </span> 也记录了程序化命令。在目标仓库中开始，并在请求修改前确认所选代理和模型。</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>opencode run <span style="color:#e6db74">"Identify this project's test command. Do not modify files."</span> </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>使用 <code>opencode run</code> 发送有边界的非交互请求。</strong> 单独确定适当的权限策略。要求不修改文件可以提供方向，但不会强制文件系统隔离。</p> <p><strong>当 shell 组合很重要时，选择这种工作流。</strong> 可重复的包装器应记录请求、退出状态、相关输出和已修改文件。明确处理失败。空 diff 和成功消息与经过验证的修复需要不同的解释。</p> <h2 id="desktop-设置与兼容性"> <a href="#desktop-%e8%ae%be%e7%bd%ae%e4%b8%8e%e5%85%bc%e5%ae%b9%e6%80%a7" title="Desktop 设置与兼容性">Desktop 设置与兼容性</a> <a href="#desktop-%e8%ae%be%e7%bd%ae%e4%b8%8e%e5%85%bc%e5%ae%b9%e6%80%a7" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Desktop 设置与兼容性">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>为目标版本使用官方下载页面。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="OpenCode 下载页面"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/download"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/download" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >OpenCode 下载页面</a> </span> 列出终端和桌面软件包。在本次检查中，下载页面宣传 v2 终端软件包，而通用文档还包含较旧的安装示例。记录客户端和后端的确切版本，不要混用不同发布轨道的说明。</p> <p><strong>用一个小型真实任务评估桌面交互。</strong> 打开项目，确认服务器，提交有边界的请求，检查已修改文件，并请求修正。评估理解代理操作所需的工作量。不要假设图形客户端完全替代编辑器和调试器。</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Desktop 试用</th> <th>预期证据</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>项目选择</strong></td> <td>代理识别目标仓库</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>模型选择</strong></td> <td>提供商和模型与试用记录一致</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>命令执行</strong></td> <td>所需运行时和测试可用</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>变更检查</strong></td> <td>容易找到并审查完整补丁</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>重启</strong></td> <td>目标项目和会话仍可识别</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="配置与模型访问"> <a href="#%e9%85%8d%e7%bd%ae%e4%b8%8e%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e8%ae%bf%e9%97%ae" title="配置与模型访问">配置与模型访问</a> <a href="#%e9%85%8d%e7%bd%ae%e4%b8%8e%e6%a8%a1%e5%9e%8b%e8%ae%bf%e9%97%ae" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="配置与模型访问">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>OpenCode 会合并多个位置的配置。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="配置参考"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/config/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >配置参考</a> </span> 解释优先级和无冲突设置的保留方式。比较有效的模型、代理和权限，而不只是一个项目文件。</p> <p><strong>提供商访问属于执行设置。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="提供商指南"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >提供商指南</a> </span> 介绍支持的服务和兼容的 endpoints。凭据、endpoint 可达性和模型工具支持都很重要。在其他位置运行的服务器需要自己有效访问提供商和仓库。</p> <p><strong>客户端不会决定总推理成本。</strong> 用相同模型和任务比较计费使用量。包括由配置错误导致的重复运行。使用本地推理时，记录系统内存、模型格式、上下文大小和运行时设置。不要把桌面下载描述成托管计算的免费替代品。</p> <h2 id="会话与安全切换"> <a href="#%e4%bc%9a%e8%af%9d%e4%b8%8e%e5%ae%89%e5%85%a8%e5%88%87%e6%8d%a2" title="会话与安全切换">会话与安全切换</a> <a href="#%e4%bc%9a%e8%af%9d%e4%b8%8e%e5%ae%89%e5%85%a8%e5%88%87%e6%8d%a2" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="会话与安全切换">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>验证连续性，不要假设连续性。</strong> 切换客户端前记录活动项目和会话。检查目标是否连接到预期服务器并显示预期历史记录。开始新会话时，提供包含目标、已完成工作和剩余检查的简要交接。</p> <p><strong>避免对同一 checkout 进行并发编辑。</strong> 两个计划不同的对话如果指向同一目录，就会共享文件。独立实验使用不同的 worktree 或 checkout。合并变更前先审查。</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Handover record </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Goal: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Current branch and working directory: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Files changed: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Checks already completed: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Known failures: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Next approved action: </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>这份记录让交接可检查。</strong> 它也能帮助区分界面问题、缺少指令和环境不匹配。不要把凭据放入记录。</p> <h2 id="服务器访问与权限"> <a href="#%e6%9c%8d%e5%8a%a1%e5%99%a8%e8%ae%bf%e9%97%ae%e4%b8%8e%e6%9d%83%e9%99%90" title="服务器访问与权限">服务器访问与权限</a> <a href="#%e6%9c%8d%e5%8a%a1%e5%99%a8%e8%ae%bf%e9%97%ae%e4%b8%8e%e6%9d%83%e9%99%90" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="服务器访问与权限">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>将代理服务器视为执行服务。</strong> 服务器文档介绍通过 <code>OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD</code> 进行可选身份验证。在跨设备连接前，有意配置访问权限。可访问的代理服务器不等于无害的静态网站。</p> <p><strong>单独审查工具权限。</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="权限指南"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/"> <a href="https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >权限指南</a> </span> 定义 allow、ask 和 deny 行为。在界面试用期间应用相同策略。检查有效规则前，不要因为客户端提示更少就认为它更安全或更有能力。</p> <p><strong>从无害的策略测试开始。</strong> 在一次性项目中请求允许的文件检查和禁止的编辑。验证观察到的行为，再进行有边界的实施。这样可以测试权限假设。</p> <h2 id="故障排除与选择"> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e9%99%a4%e4%b8%8e%e9%80%89%e6%8b%a9" title="故障排除与选择">故障排除与选择</a> <a href="#%e6%95%85%e9%9a%9c%e6%8e%92%e9%99%a4%e4%b8%8e%e9%80%89%e6%8b%a9" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="故障排除与选择">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>症状</th> <th>首先检查</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Desktop 连接失败</strong></td> <td>所选服务器和本地 sidecar 状态</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>一个客户端缺少模型</strong></td> <td>服务器版本、提供商访问和配置</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>测试结果不同</strong></td> <td>项目目录和运行时环境</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>缺少对话</strong></td> <td>服务器和会话身份</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>加载插件前正常</strong></td> <td>插件配置和版本兼容性</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p><strong>如果脚本请求和 shell 上下文让工作更简单，就选择终端。</strong> <strong>如果图形化项目导航改善监督，就选择 Desktop。</strong> 将提供商和策略决定与这个偏好分开。</p> <p><strong>下一步：</strong> 在 <span itemscope item.title: Which AI Models Can Run on a Raspberry Pi 4 or 5?
item.category: "Raspberry Pi" , "Artificial Intelligence" , "Self Hosting"
item.description: Use measured Raspberry Pi 4 and 5 results to choose local language models by memory, speed, and workload, from tiny LFM2.5 models to 3B and larger options.
item.content:encoded: <p>A Raspberry Pi can run a useful language model locally, but the model must fit the board’s memory and the response time your application can tolerate. A 2 GB Raspberry Pi 4 is best suited to models below about one billion parameters. An 8 GB Raspberry Pi 5 can run compact 1B–3B models comfortably and load some larger quantized models with substantial compromises.</p> <p>We benchmarked these models ourselves through Ollama on a <strong>2 GB Pi 4B</strong> and an <strong>8 GB Pi 5</strong>, both using microSD storage. The runs behind the tables used the same five short assistant prompts, system prompt, fixed seed, and 140-token output cap. We unloaded other models before each run and measured cold-load time, time to first visible token, total reply time, output speed, and peak resident memory. These were single-pass tests of a short-reply workload, so the results are sizing examples rather than universal speed or answer-quality rankings. The Pi 5’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Cortex-A76 CPU and available memory configurations"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-5/"> <a href="https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/raspberry-pi-5/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Cortex-A76 CPU and available memory configurations</a> </span> also differ materially from the Pi 4’s <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Cortex-A72 platform"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/545-raspberry-pi-4-model-b/documents/RP-008341-DS-1-raspberry-pi-4-datasheet.pdf"> <a href="https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/545-raspberry-pi-4-model-b/documents/RP-008341-DS-1-raspberry-pi-4-datasheet.pdf" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Cortex-A72 platform</a> </span> .</p> <h2 id="the-model-types-that-make-sense"> <a href="#the-model-types-that-make-sense" title="The model types that make sense">The model types that make sense</a> <a href="#the-model-types-that-make-sense" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="The model types that make sense">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Kind of model</th> <th>Examples from the measurements</th> <th>Practical use</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Tiny text models, about 230M–600M parameters</td> <td>LFM2.5-230M, LFM2.5-350M, Qwen2.5-0.5B</td> <td>Short local commands, summaries, and constrained question answering; the best starting point for a 2 GB Pi 4</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Compact text models, about 1B–2B</td> <td>LFM2.5-1.2B, Qwen2.5-1.5B, Gemma 3 1B, MiniCPM5-1B</td> <td>More room for nuanced instructions on a Pi 5 or a higher-memory Pi 4, with slower replies than the tiniest models</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Quantized 3B–4B text models</td> <td>Qwen2.5-3B, Llama 3.2 3B, Gemma 3 4B</td> <td>More capable candidates for an 8 GB Pi 5 when a wait of several seconds per reply is acceptable</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Larger sparse or hybrid models</td> <td>LFM2.5 8B</td> <td>Technically runnable on the tested 8 GB Pi 5, but with a large memory footprint and long cold load</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>These are <strong>text-generation</strong> results. They do not establish performance for image generation, speech recognition, vision, or training. “Runs” also means more than fitting the model file on a card: the runtime, context cache, operating system, and other services need RAM. Quantization reduces the weight file size, but it can reduce answer quality, especially at extreme settings such as 1-bit weights.</p> <h3 id="what-our-numbers-measure"> <a href="#what-our-numbers-measure" title="What our numbers measure">What our numbers measure</a> <a href="#what-our-numbers-measure" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What our numbers measure">#</a> </h3> <p>The benchmark sent short factual, procedural safety, retrieved-context, weather, and help prompts to Ollama’s chat API. Each model saw the same prompt set and seed. Before timing a model, we unloaded it so the next request would include a cold load; the reported <strong>wall time</strong> is the complete request, while <strong>tokens per second</strong> describes only output generation. We also recorded the first <em>visible</em> token, which matters when a model spends time reasoning before it answers.</p> <p>For memory, we sampled the Pi’s available RAM and swap alongside the resident memory of Ollama and its inference process during each request. The <strong>RSS</strong> figures below are process-resident memory, not the entire host’s memory demand. File-backed pages, the operating system, a browser, or another local service can still make a nominally fitting model swap. The tables use the original five-prompt, single-pass runs. We later extended the harness with a news prompt and reply-rule checks; those checks clarify what to look for, but they do not turn the earlier timings into six-prompt compliance results.</p> <p>Neither tokens per second nor parameter count is a quality score. A model can emit text quickly yet omit a requested source, exceed a word budget, or produce an unfinished sentence. We would compare models on the prompts we actually plan to send, then inspect their answers before choosing one for an application.</p> <h2 id="raspberry-pi-4-favor-the-smallest-models"> <a href="#raspberry-pi-4-favor-the-smallest-models" title="Raspberry Pi 4: favor the smallest models">Raspberry Pi 4: favor the smallest models</a> <a href="#raspberry-pi-4-favor-the-smallest-models" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Raspberry Pi 4: favor the smallest models">#</a> </h2> <p>The tested 2 GB Pi 4 had limited headroom. The smallest LFM2.5 models completed all five prompts, as did <code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code>. They are sensible choices for brief offline replies or a small local assistant.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th style="text-align: right">Model file</th> <th style="text-align: right">Measured output speed</th> <th style="text-align: right">Average reply time</th> <th>Observed memory or outcome</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>LFM2.5-230M, imported GGUF</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.25 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">12.8 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">7.2 s</td> <td>383 MB peak resident memory; 5/5 prompts</td> </tr> <tr> <td>LFM2.5-350M, imported GGUF</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.38 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.6 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.6 s</td> <td>516 MB peak resident memory; 5/5 prompts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.40 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.0 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">9.7 s</td> <td>5/5 prompts; available directly in Ollama</td> </tr> <tr> <td>MiniCPM5-1B, imported GGUF, reasoning off</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.69 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.9 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">12.2 s</td> <td>883 MB peak resident memory; 5/5 prompts</td> </tr> <tr> <td>MiniCPM5-1B, imported GGUF, default reasoning</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.69 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.7 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">33.3 s</td> <td>Only 1/5 prompts returned a useful visible reply</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3:0.6b</code>, default reasoning</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.52 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">6.4 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">40.4 s</td> <td>One empty reply; board rebooted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>granite4:350m</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.71 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">4.6 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">15.5 s</td> <td>913 MB RSS, no swap or reboot; slow but stable</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>gemma3:1b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.82 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">4.0 tokens/s</td> <td style="text-align: right">30.7 s</td> <td>Heavy swapping; board rebooted during testing</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3.5:0.8b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">1.04 GB</td> <td style="text-align: right">—</td> <td style="text-align: right">—</td> <td>Did not complete; board rebooted</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The Pi 4 results are especially sensitive to the rest of the system. We observed board resets during larger-model tests, including a <code>qwen3.5:0.8b</code> run that never completed. That is evidence about our 2 GB setup, rather than a claim that every Pi 4 or every 1B model will reboot. A 4 GB or 8 GB Pi 4 has more memory, but its CPU will still make inference slower than on the tested Pi 5. We did not directly benchmark those Pi 4 memory variants.</p> <p>One early Pi 4 pass also appeared much worse than the final measurements: roughly 625 MB of staged GGUF files sat in a RAM-backed <code>/tmp</code>, leaving only about 500–600 MB free and pushing hundreds of megabytes into swap. After moving those files to persistent storage, the small-model results above gave a more useful picture of inference memory. On a 2 GB board, even the <em>location of a download</em> can distort a benchmark.</p> <p><strong>Recommendation:</strong> The imported LFM2.5-350M is our default for this 2 GB board. It remained stable at <strong>516 MB RSS</strong>, left about <strong>1 GB of RAM available</strong>, and passed <strong>5/6</strong> reply-rule checks in the Pi 4 compliance pass. It did miss source names in repeated Pi 5 testing, so applications that require attribution should check for it. Choose LFM2.5-230M when latency and memory headroom matter most: it was faster and lighter, but in one medical-context answer it garbled “nausea or vomiting” into “nausea/ventilator use.” That content error makes it a weaker default for safety or health replies despite its higher repeated mechanical compliance score. Choose <code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code> if you need a model from the <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Ollama registry"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://ollama.com/library/qwen2.5/tags"> <a href="https://ollama.com/library/qwen2.5/tags" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Ollama registry</a> </span> , while accounting for its weaker instruction compliance. <code>granite4:350m</code> stayed stable but took longer and used more memory; MiniCPM5-1B is viable only when the client disables reasoning. Avoid Gemma 3 1B and Qwen3.5 0.8B on this specific 2 GB setup because our runs triggered resets.</p> <h2 id="raspberry-pi-5-more-choice-with-a-speed-tradeoff"> <a href="#raspberry-pi-5-more-choice-with-a-speed-tradeoff" title="Raspberry Pi 5: more choice, with a speed tradeoff">Raspberry Pi 5: more choice, with a speed tradeoff</a> <a href="#raspberry-pi-5-more-choice-with-a-speed-tradeoff" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Raspberry Pi 5: more choice, with a speed tradeoff">#</a> </h2> <p>The 8 GB Pi 5 handled all <strong>25 models</strong> in our speed-and-memory benchmark. The table includes every run, including models we do not recommend for this short-reply workload. A dagger marks an imported GGUF. “Think off” records the setting used for the speed run; the separate compliance pass did not necessarily use that setting.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th style="text-align: right">File GB</th> <th style="text-align: right">Output tok/s</th> <th style="text-align: right">Reply s</th> <th style="text-align: right">Peak RSS MB</th> <th>Short-reply assessment</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><code>lfm2.5-230m</code> †</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.25</td> <td style="text-align: right">45.0</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.8</td> <td style="text-align: right">446</td> <td>Lowest latency; 78% repeated compliance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>bonsai-1.7b</code> †, Q1_0</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.25</td> <td style="text-align: right">15.3</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.2</td> <td style="text-align: right">871</td> <td>Skip: 1-bit weights and 3/6 single-pass compliance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>lfm2.5-350m</code> †</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.38</td> <td style="text-align: right">30.0</td> <td style="text-align: right">2.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">581</td> <td>Fast, but missed source citation in 5/18 repeats</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.40</td> <td style="text-align: right">28.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">3.6</td> <td style="text-align: right">675</td> <td>Easy registry option; 61% repeated compliance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3:0.6b</code>, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.52</td> <td style="text-align: right">23.0</td> <td style="text-align: right">4.3</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,069</td> <td>Conditional: 4/6 compliance pass, reasoning setting matters</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>bonsai-4b</code> †, Q1_0</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.57</td> <td style="text-align: right">6.8</td> <td style="text-align: right">18.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,343</td> <td>Experimental 1-bit model; 6/6 single pass is unconfirmed</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>minicpm5-1b</code> †, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.69</td> <td style="text-align: right">18.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">869</td> <td>Conditional: default reasoning gave empty replies</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>granite4:350m</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.71</td> <td style="text-align: right">12.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">6.6</td> <td style="text-align: right">892</td> <td>Fits, but slower and larger than small LFM2.5</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>lfm2.5-1.2b</code> †</td> <td style="text-align: right">0.73</td> <td style="text-align: right">15.5</td> <td style="text-align: right">4.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">967</td> <td>Best overall for our workload; 89% repeated compliance</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>llama3.2:1b-instruct-q4_K_M</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.81</td> <td style="text-align: right">13.0</td> <td style="text-align: right">7.5</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,244</td> <td>Registry alternative; 5/6 compliance pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>gemma3:1b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.82</td> <td style="text-align: right">11.2</td> <td style="text-align: right">10.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,262</td> <td>Best registry-only repeated compliance: 83%</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct-q4_K_M</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">0.99</td> <td style="text-align: right">10.3</td> <td style="text-align: right">9.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,361</td> <td>4/6 compliance pass; Gemma 3 1B followed rules better</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3.5:0.8b</code>, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.04</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.8</td> <td style="text-align: right">12.2</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,592</td> <td>0/6 with default reasoning; avoid without thinking control</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>spark-x2.5-1.7b</code> †, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.11</td> <td style="text-align: right">9.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">9.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,542</td> <td>0/6 with default reasoning; avoid without thinking control</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3:1.7b</code>, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.36</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">12.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,867</td> <td>Conditional; more memory and delay than smaller choices</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>minicpm5-2b</code> †, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">1.56</td> <td style="text-align: right">7.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">10.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">1,787</td> <td>Conditional; 5/6 single pass, extra bullets</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen2.5:3b-instruct-q4_K_M</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">1.93</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.2</td> <td style="text-align: right">14.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">2,366</td> <td>Trial 3B option; 5/6 single pass</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>granite4:micro-h</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">1.94</td> <td style="text-align: right">3.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">23.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">2,486</td> <td>Skip for interactive use: slow decode</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>llama3.2:3b-instruct-q4_K_M</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">2.02</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.5</td> <td style="text-align: right">18.6</td> <td style="text-align: right">2,831</td> <td>Alternative 3B trial; no compliance run reported</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>granite4:micro</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">2.10</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.3</td> <td style="text-align: right">17.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">2,679</td> <td>Fits, but slower replies than smaller alternatives</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen3.5:2b</code>, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">2.74</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.0</td> <td style="text-align: right">16.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">3,627</td> <td>High memory and delay; no compliance run reported</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>gemma3:4b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">3.34</td> <td style="text-align: right">3.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">30.3</td> <td style="text-align: right">4,267</td> <td>Skip for responsive replies; 14.3 s to first token</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>ling-3.0-tiny</code> †, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">4.82</td> <td style="text-align: right">9.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">19.4</td> <td style="text-align: right">5,071</td> <td>Large footprint; 5/6 single pass with grounding failure</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>lfm2.5:8b</code>, think off</td> <td style="text-align: right">5.16</td> <td style="text-align: right">8.7</td> <td style="text-align: right">54.6</td> <td style="text-align: right">5,317</td> <td>Fits tightly; 34.4 s cold load and overlong answers</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>gemma3n:e2b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">5.62</td> <td style="text-align: right">6.1</td> <td style="text-align: right">25.9</td> <td style="text-align: right">5,261</td> <td>Skip: swap pressure alongside other Pi services</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>† Imported GGUF. Reply times and memory figures are from the five-prompt Pi 5 speed run; compliance figures come from separate six-prompt tests. A model without a compliance score was not shown to obey the reply rules.</p> <p>The small LFM2.5 models were the fastest <em>for this short-reply workload</em>. The 1.2B version offers a practical middle ground on the tested Pi 5. Gemma 3 1B is a registry-only alternative with better repeated reply-rule compliance than Qwen2.5 1.5B in our later tests. A 3B model may be worth the slower output for prompts that need more capacity, but these timings alone do not prove which model gives the best answers.</p> <p>Cold-load and first-token delays change the experience. LFM2.5-230M loaded in about <strong>0.21 seconds</strong> and produced a visible token in <strong>0.37 seconds</strong> on the Pi 5. Qwen2.5 1.5B took <strong>2.59 seconds</strong> to load and <strong>3.66 seconds</strong> to its first visible token; Qwen2.5 3B took <strong>5.60</strong> and <strong>7.97 seconds</strong>, respectively. For an occasional question, those delays may matter more than the output rate once generation begins. For a continuously loaded model, they matter less, but keeping a model resident consumes memory between requests.</p> <p>Other measured candidates illustrate why we do not rank by parameter count alone. With reasoning disabled, <code>qwen3:0.6b</code> reached <strong>23.0 tokens/s</strong> on the Pi 5 at <strong>1,069 MB RSS</strong>, while imported MiniCPM5-1B reached <strong>18.4 tokens/s</strong> at <strong>869 MB RSS</strong>. <code>granite4:350m</code> needed a <strong>0.71 GB</strong> download and generated <strong>12.1 tokens/s</strong>, despite its 350M label. Model packaging and architecture change the relationship between name, file size, memory, and speed.</p> <p>If your client can reliably send <code>think: false</code>, Qwen3 0.6B and MiniCPM5-1B are reasonable experiments when you want alternatives to LFM2.5. MiniCPM5-2B, Qwen3 1.7B, and Spark-X2.5 1.7B also ran on the Pi 5, but none offered a clear speed-and-memory advantage over our primary choices. The compliance test used default reasoning for MiniCPM5-1B and Spark-X2.5; its empty replies should not be presented as the outcome of their think-off speed runs. Conversely, a fast think-off timing does not establish that a bridge which omits that flag will receive a usable answer.</p> <p>If installation simplicity matters more than raw speed, Gemma 3 1B and Llama 3.2 1B are plausible registry choices on the 8 GB Pi 5. Gemma 3 1B followed the tested reply rules in <strong>15/18</strong> repeated replies. Llama 3.2 1B passed <strong>5/6</strong> in one pass, so its compliance estimate is less certain. Qwen2.5 1.5B loaded and answered faster than Gemma 3 1B in our timing run, but passed only <strong>4/6</strong> reply-rule checks in its single compliance pass. Choose between them using the requirement that matters to your own prompts.</p> <p>For occasional longer or harder text prompts, the quantized Qwen2.5 3B and Llama 3.2 3B are the 3B candidates with manageable memory use on our 8 GB Pi 5. We measured their speed and memory, and Qwen2.5 3B passed <strong>5/6</strong> in one compliance pass; we did not publish a comparable compliance run for Llama 3.2 3B. Their larger parameter counts are a reason to <em>test</em> them on tasks where smaller models fall short, not proof that they answered those tasks better. Granite 4 Micro and Micro-H, Qwen3.5 2B, Gemma 3 4B, Ling-3.0-tiny, and Gemma 3n E2B all fit or loaded in our Pi 5 trials, but offered less attractive latency, memory headroom, or reply reliability for this short-response application.</p> <p>The two Bonsai models demonstrate the cost of extreme quantization. Their Q1_0 files were strikingly small for 1.7B and 4B parameter names, yet the 1.7B model passed only <strong>3/6</strong> reply-rule checks. The 4B model passed a single six-prompt compliance pass, but took <strong>18.1 seconds</strong> per reply and has no repeated compliance confirmation. We would treat both as experiments rather than default recommendations, especially where answer quality matters.</p> <p>The 8B LFM2.5 result needs context: its hybrid design uses fewer active parameters per token, so its decode rate exceeded the measured 3B dense models. It still took <strong>34.4 seconds to load cold</strong> from microSD and used over <strong>5.3 GB resident memory</strong>. It is a demonstration of what fits, not a comfortable default for a Pi that also runs other services. The measured <code>gemma3n:e2b</code> similarly used about 5.3 GB resident memory and caused swapping alongside the other services on the test host.</p> <p>The LFM2.5 8B run also reached the full <strong>140-token cap</strong> instead of keeping its response brief. The 4B Gemma 3 run took <strong>14.3 seconds</strong> to its first token and <strong>30.3 seconds</strong> for the complete reply. Both can be loaded on this Pi 5, but neither behaved like a responsive small assistant in our tests. A tiny model with an appropriately short answer may serve a radio or command interface better than a larger model with a faster decode rate on paper.</p> <h2 id="memory-reasoning-and-model-format"> <a href="#memory-reasoning-and-model-format" title="Memory, reasoning, and model format">Memory, reasoning, and model format</a> <a href="#memory-reasoning-and-model-format" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Memory, reasoning, and model format">#</a> </h2> <p>A useful first estimate from our measurements is <strong>model download size × 1.4</strong> for resident inference memory. It is only a rule of thumb: context length, runtime settings, model architecture, and other processes can change the requirement. Check available memory while generating, keep only one model loaded on a small host, and leave room for the OS. A 4 GB board can reasonably start with the tiny or compact models, but our 4 GB recommendations are extrapolations rather than direct 4 GB tests.</p> <p>For example, a 0.73 GB LFM2.5-1.2B file corresponded to about <strong>967 MB RSS</strong> on the Pi 5, while the 0.99 GB Qwen2.5 1.5B file reached <strong>1,361 MB RSS</strong>. The rule works reasonably for those models, but it is not a hard limit. Plan for more than the measured model process if the Pi also runs an interface, search index, local library, or other background service. Watch swap use during a real request; a model that technically loads while constantly swapping is not a practical fit.</p> <p>Some models generate an internal reasoning block before their visible answer. In our tests, <code>qwen3:0.6b</code> on the 2 GB Pi 4 took much longer to produce visible text, and MiniCPM5-1B answered only one of five prompts with its default reasoning setting versus five of five with reasoning disabled. For a short response budget, set <code>think: false</code> in a compatible Ollama API request, or select a model that does not default to reasoning. This setting applies to supported models and clients; it is not a universal speed switch.</p> <p>The distinction matters because a token cap can include tokens spent on reasoning even when the user sees no answer. On the Pi 4, default-thinking <code>qwen3:0.6b</code> averaged <strong>40.4 seconds per request</strong>, and one prompt produced an empty visible reply. MiniCPM5-1B averaged <strong>33.3 seconds</strong> with its default setting versus <strong>12.2 seconds</strong> with reasoning disabled. We also disabled reasoning for the Pi 5 runs of Qwen3, Qwen3.5, MiniCPM5, Ling-3.0, and Spark-X2.5 where indicated in our records. Compare a model under the exact reasoning setting your client will use.</p> <h3 id="check-whether-the-reply-is-usable"> <a href="#check-whether-the-reply-is-usable" title="Check whether the reply is usable">Check whether the reply is usable</a> <a href="#check-whether-the-reply-is-usable" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Check whether the reply is usable">#</a> </h3> <p>For our short mesh-assistant workload, the response contract is as important as speed: at most <strong>90 words</strong>, no more than <strong>three bullets</strong>, plain text, a finished sentence, and use of supplied retrieval context with its source named. The bridge divides text into <strong>180-character chunks</strong>. A long answer occupies more radio airtime, even if the model generated it quickly.</p> <p>The later version of our benchmark checks for empty replies, a prompt-specific word limit, too many bullets, Markdown tables or code fences, an unfinished ending, missing terms from supplied context, and a missing source name. When we scored replies against the deployed assistant prompt, small models breached these rules regularly. The most consequential failures were <strong>empty replies</strong> when reasoning consumed the token budget, followed by answers that ignored retrieved context or omitted its source. Going over the word limit or using too many bullets still delivered visible text, but wasted airtime. These are mechanical checks, not a substitute for reading the answer: they cannot establish factual accuracy or whether safety advice is sound.</p> <h4 id="repeated-pi-5-compliance-results"> <a href="#repeated-pi-5-compliance-results" title="Repeated Pi 5 compliance results">Repeated Pi 5 compliance results</a> <a href="#repeated-pi-5-compliance-results" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Repeated Pi 5 compliance results">#</a> </h4> <p>We first ran six prompts once per model with a <strong>220-token cap</strong> and the deployed system prompt. Models that looked plausible were then tested twice more with a different seed, giving <strong>18 replies per model</strong>. A perfect single pass did not guarantee a perfect repeat. The repeated results below provide a firmer comparison for the short mesh replies we tested:</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Model</th> <th style="text-align: right">Replies that followed all checked rules</th> <th>Main observed failures</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Imported LFM2.5-1.2B</td> <td style="text-align: right">16/18 (89%)</td> <td>Two unfinished replies</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>gemma3:1b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">15/18 (83%)</td> <td>Three unfinished replies</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Imported LFM2.5-230M</td> <td style="text-align: right">14/18 (78%)</td> <td>Unfinished replies and missing source names</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Imported LFM2.5-350M</td> <td style="text-align: right">13/18 (72%)</td> <td>Missing source names</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code></td> <td style="text-align: right">11/18 (61%)</td> <td>Too many bullets, excess words, missing source names</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>On the <strong>2 GB Pi 4</strong>, the separate six-prompt compliance pass found <strong>5/6</strong> for LFM2.5-350M, <strong>4/6</strong> for LFM2.5-230M, and <strong>2/6</strong> for Qwen2.5-0.5B. MiniCPM5-1B improved from <strong>1/6</strong> with default reasoning to <strong>5/6</strong> with reasoning disabled. These Pi 4 scores are single-pass results, so we give more weight to the repeated Pi 5 results when discussing general instruction-following behavior, while using the Pi 4 runs to judge stability and speed on that board.</p> <p>The failures have different consequences. An <strong>empty</strong> reply gives the user nothing; an answer that ignores supplied material can be misleading. A missing source name prevents readers from checking attribution. Extra bullets or words mainly consume additional 180-character packets. An unfinished sentence may indicate truncation. The LFM2.5-230M medical-term error is a reminder that a reply can pass these mechanical checks and still be wrong. None of the five repeated candidates followed every rule in all 18 replies, so an application that requires a strict length or format should enforce it after generation as well and review high-stakes content separately.</p> <p>We also checked the actual bridge endpoint, Ollama’s OpenAI-compatible <code>/v1/chat/completions</code>, with retrieved WikiMed context. On the Pi 5, LFM2.5-1.2B returned a 28-word answer using six supplied terms; Qwen2.5-0.5B returned 38 words using seven. Both fit within two 180-character packets. That endpoint check confirms the imported LFM2.5 model works through the bridge’s request path, but one successful answer is not a reliability guarantee.</p> <p>Ollama publishes many ready-to-pull models, including <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Qwen2.5’s 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B variants"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://ollama.com/library/qwen2.5/tags"> <a href="https://ollama.com/library/qwen2.5/tags" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Qwen2.5’s 0.5B, 1.5B, and 3B variants</a> </span> . We imported the small LFM2.5 models from <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Liquid AI’s GGUF releases"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M-GGUF/tree/main"> <a href="https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M-GGUF/tree/main" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Liquid AI’s GGUF releases</a> </span> into Ollama. Check the exact tag or GGUF filename before downloading: model registries and repositories can change. Keep GGUF downloads on persistent storage; in our tests, staging files in a RAM-backed <code>/tmp</code> consumed scarce Pi 4 memory.</p> <h3 id="registry-tags-and-gguf-imports"> <a href="#registry-tags-and-gguf-imports" title="Registry tags and GGUF imports">Registry tags and GGUF imports</a> <a href="#registry-tags-and-gguf-imports" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Registry tags and GGUF imports">#</a> </h3> <p>An Ollama tag is the shortest path to a first test: pull the exact tag and run it. The small LFM2.5 models in our tables were <strong>GGUF imports</strong>, not tags named <code>lfm2.5-230m</code>, <code>lfm2.5-350m</code>, or <code>lfm2.5-1.2b</code> in Ollama’s public library. GGUF is a model-file format; names such as <code>Q8_0</code> and <code>Q4_K_M</code> identify quantization choices. The 230M and 350M LFM2.5 files we used were Q8_0, while the 1.2B file was Q4_K_M. Consequently, the same parameter count downloaded in another quantization may not have the same file size, memory use, or quality.</p> <p>To import the tested 350M variant, download its GGUF to a directory on persistent storage, create a Modelfile pointing to it, and let Ollama copy it into its model store:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>mkdir -p <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$HOME<span style="color:#e6db74">/gguf"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>cd <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$HOME<span style="color:#e6db74">/gguf"</span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>curl -fL -C - --retry <span style="color:#ae81ff">5</span> --retry-all-errors -O <span style="color:#ae81ff">\ </span></span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M-GGUF/resolve/main/LFM2.5-350M-Q8_0.gguf </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>printf <span style="color:#e6db74">'FROM %s/LFM2.5-350M-Q8_0.gguf\n'</span> <span style="color:#e6db74">"</span>$PWD<span style="color:#e6db74">"</span> > Modelfile-lfm2.5-350m </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama create lfm2.5-350m -f Modelfile-lfm2.5-350m </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama run lfm2.5-350m </span></span></code></pre></div><p>The import temporarily needs space for both the downloaded file and Ollama’s stored copy. We used resumable downloads because long GGUF transfers sometimes broke mid-file. Before importing a downloaded GGUF, compare its SHA-256 with the file hash published by its source; a partial transfer can otherwise look like a model problem. On our Pi setup, <code>/tmp</code> was RAM-backed, so staging a GGUF there reduced the memory available for inference.</p> <h2 id="a-practical-starting-point"> <a href="#a-practical-starting-point" title="A practical starting point">A practical starting point</a> <a href="#a-practical-starting-point" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="A practical starting point">#</a> </h2> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Hardware and goal</th> <th>First model to try</th> <th>Why</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>2 GB Pi 4, default</td> <td>Imported LFM2.5-350M</td> <td>Stable at 516 MB RSS with about 1 GB available; selected after a medical-term error from 230M</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2 GB Pi 4, lowest latency</td> <td>Imported LFM2.5-230M</td> <td>383 MB RSS and 7.2-second average reply; verify content carefully, especially for health or safety questions</td> </tr> <tr> <td>2 GB Pi 4, registry-only</td> <td><code>qwen2.5:0.5b</code></td> <td>Direct Ollama pull and stable in our five-prompt Pi 4 run; 61% repeated compliance on the Pi 5</td> </tr> <tr> <td>4 GB Pi 4 or Pi 5</td> <td>Imported LFM2.5-1.2B, then test locally</td> <td>967 MB RSS and 89% repeated compliance on our 8 GB Pi 5; we did not benchmark 4 GB variants directly</td> </tr> <tr> <td>8 GB Pi 5, responsive assistant</td> <td>Imported LFM2.5-1.2B</td> <td>15.5 tokens/s, 4.7-second total reply, and the highest repeated compliance we measured</td> </tr> <tr> <td>8 GB Pi 5, registry-only setup</td> <td><code>gemma3:1b</code></td> <td>11.2 tokens/s, 1,262 MB RSS, and 83% repeated compliance</td> </tr> <tr> <td>8 GB Pi 5, try a larger text model</td> <td>Quantized Qwen2.5 3B or Llama 3.2 3B</td> <td>Both ran at about 5 tokens/s and used 2.4–2.8 GB RSS; Qwen2.5 3B passed 5/6 in a single compliance pass</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>These choices prioritize short, useful replies on a Pi that may also run other services. They are starting points rather than claims that one model is best at every task. In our single-pass Pi 5 compliance check, default-thinking <code>qwen3.5:0.8b</code> and Spark-X2.5 returned no compliant replies, while MiniCPM5-1B managed 1/6; a client that cannot disable their reasoning should avoid them for this short-reply workload. We would test the final model with the actual prompt, context length, concurrency, and response limit planned for deployment.</p> <p>For the registry model, after <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="installing Ollama for Linux"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://ollama.com/download/linux"> <a href="https://ollama.com/download/linux" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >installing Ollama for Linux</a> </span> , run:</p> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-bash" data-lang="bash"><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama pull qwen2.5:0.5b </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>ollama run qwen2.5:0.5b </span></span></code></pre></div><p>Test with your own prompts, desired answer length, and other services running. Record both total reply time and memory use. That will tell you more about whether a model belongs on your Pi than its parameter count alone.</p> <p>On a memory-constrained node, keep an eye on swap while testing. If a larger model makes the board unresponsive, use a smaller model and set an Ollama service memory limit appropriate to that model so an oversized load fails instead of exhausting the host. A service cap is a safeguard, not a way to make an oversized model fit. The Pi 4 resets in our tests show why responsiveness and memory headroom belong in the selection criteria alongside tokens per second.</p> <h2 id="turn-the-benchmark-into-a-deployment-decision"> <a href="#turn-the-benchmark-into-a-deployment-decision" title="Turn the benchmark into a deployment decision">Turn the benchmark into a deployment decision</a> <a href="#turn-the-benchmark-into-a-deployment-decision" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Turn the benchmark into a deployment decision">#</a> </h2> <p>Before installing a model for daily use, write down four limits: <strong>maximum reply time, maximum resident memory, response format, and failure behavior</strong>. Test those limits with the services that will share the board. A model that passes alone but forces swap beside your radio bridge or dashboard does not meet the deployment requirement.</p> <p>Keep one small fallback model installed. Route to it when the primary model exceeds the memory limit, returns an empty reply, or fails the response contract. Record the model tag, quantization, Ollama version, prompt, context length, and seed with each comparison so a later model update does not look like a hardware improvement.</p> Read More at https://zh.simeononsecurity.com/

item.title: Docker in LXC on Proxmox: Reliability, Evidence, and VM Migration
item.category: "Virtualization" , "Linux Administration" , "Homelab"
item.description: Evaluate Docker inside Proxmox LXC with a documented AppArmor failure, a careful reading of a host-freeze report, diagnostic commands, and a VM migration plan.
item.content:encoded: <p><strong>Docker inside Linux Containers (LXC)</strong> trades some infrastructure overhead for more interactions between the application runtime and the Proxmox host. For Docker services your household depends on, a Debian <strong>virtual machine (VM)</strong> is a practical starting point because it separates the guest kernel and simplifies the environment you must reproduce during troubleshooting. This article examines the supplied video, checks its underlying incident report, and adds documented failures and a migration plan.</p> <h2 id="要点"> <a href="#%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" title="要点">要点</a> <a href="#%e8%a6%81%e7%82%b9" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="要点">#</a> </h2> <ul> <li><strong>Separate failure types:</strong> A Docker startup error, a stalled VM, and an unresponsive physical host require different investigations.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate the evidence:</strong> Stability after migration supports a recovery decision without proving the original cause.</li> <li><strong>Check current documentation:</strong> Native OCI image support and Docker nested inside LXC are different deployment paths.</li> <li><strong>Protect persistent data:</strong> Proxmox backups and Compose files do not automatically cover every application data location.</li> <li><strong>Test the recovery plan:</strong> Measure restoration, reboot behavior, and service availability before retiring the old deployment.</li> </ul> <h2 id="开始之前"> <a href="#%e5%bc%80%e5%a7%8b%e4%b9%8b%e5%89%8d" title="开始之前">开始之前</a> <a href="#%e5%bc%80%e5%a7%8b%e4%b9%8b%e5%89%8d" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="开始之前">#</a> </h2> <p><strong>Difficulty:</strong> Intermediate. <strong>Audience:</strong> Proxmox administrators choosing between nested Docker and Docker in a VM. You should recognize a Compose project, a container mount, and a Linux shell prompt before following the diagnostic examples.</p> <p><strong>Estimated effort:</strong> Allow 30–60 minutes for inventory and evidence collection. Migration time depends on database size, storage throughput, hardware access, and the outage window you choose. The examples below are documented procedures and illustrative reasoning, not benchmarks from a lab operated for this article.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Requirement</th> <th>Why it matters</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Host console access</strong></td> <td>Distinguishes network failure from a host-wide stall</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Current backups</strong></td> <td>Provides a recovery path before changing the deployment</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Container and VM IDs</strong></td> <td>Keeps host commands directed at the intended workload</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Application data inventory</strong></td> <td>Identifies volumes, bind mounts, databases, and external dependencies</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Separate test environment</strong></td> <td>Supports migration rehearsal without duplicate production writers</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2 id="watch-the-source-video"> <a href="#watch-the-source-video" title="Watch the Source Video">Watch the Source Video</a> <a href="#watch-the-source-video" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Watch the Source Video">#</a> </h2> <script> function loadLiteYouTubeScript() { if (document.querySelector('script[src^="/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js"]')) { console.log('Lite YouTube script is already loaded.'); return; } var scriptTag = document.createElement('script'); scriptTag.src = '/p/jsdelivr/npm/@justinribeiro/lite-youtube@1.5.0/lite-youtube.js'; scriptTag.setAttribute('defer', ''); scriptTag.setAttribute('type', 'module'); scriptTag.setAttribute('fetchpriority', 'low'); document.body.appendChild(scriptTag); } document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () { if (typeof yieldToMain === 'function') { yieldToMain(loadLiteYouTubeScript, "user-visible"); } else { loadLiteYouTubeScript(); } }); </script> <style scoped> .lite-youtube-fallback { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; flex-direction: column; gap: 1em; padding: 1em; background-color: #000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .lite-youtube-fallback::before { display: block; content: ''; border: solid transparent; border-width: 2em 0 2em 3em; border-left-color: red; } .lite-youtube-fallback:hover::before { border-left-color: #fff; } .lite-youtube-fallback:focus { outline: 2px solid red; } </style><div itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/VideoObject http://schema.org/LearningResource" style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC"> <meta itemprop="description" content="An explainer about Docker nested inside Proxmox LXC, intermittent host freezes, and a migration to Debian virtual machines"> <meta itemprop="thumbnailUrl" content="https://img.youtube.com/vi/XyPBHhZg0Ok/maxresdefault.jpg"> <meta itemprop="contentUrl" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyPBHhZg0Ok"> <meta itemprop="uploadDate" content="2026-09-15T17:00:09-07:00"> <meta itemprop="learningResourceType" content="Concept Overview"> <meta itemprop="educationalLevel" content="High school (US)"> <lite-youtube videoid="XyPBHhZg0Ok" videotitle="Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC" videoplay="" nocookie posterloading="lazy" loading="lazy" params=""> <noscript> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyPBHhZg0Ok" class="lite-youtube-fallback" style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; border:0;" title="Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC"> <span class="lyt-visually-hidden"></span> </a> </noscript> </lite-youtube> </div> <script type="application/ld+json"> { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": ["VideoObject", "LearningResource"], "name": "Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC", "description": "An explainer about Docker nested inside Proxmox LXC, intermittent host freezes, and a migration to Debian virtual machines", "thumbnailUrl": ["https:\/\/img.youtube.com\/vi\/XyPBHhZg0Ok\/maxresdefault.jpg"], "contentUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyPBHhZg0Ok", "uploadDate": "2026-09-15T17:00:09-07:00", "learningResourceType": "Concept Overview", "educationalLevel": "High school (US)" } </script> <p><strong>Source video:</strong> <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyPBHhZg0Ok"> <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XyPBHhZg0Ok" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Proxmox: The Hidden Danger of Running Docker Inside LXC</a> </span> , published September 15, 2026, by <em>Proxmox x Kubernetes x Homelab x Backup</em>. The central question is useful: how much operational uncertainty accompanies a resource-saving architecture?</p> <p><strong>Evidence boundary:</strong> The video narrates an incident and proposes lessons. The sections below distinguish the owner’s observations, documented software behavior, and recommendations derived from them.</p> <h2 id="what-the-incident-establishes"> <a href="#what-the-incident-establishes" title="What the Incident Establishes">What the Incident Establishes</a> <a href="#what-the-incident-establishes" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="What the Incident Establishes">#</a> </h2> <p>The original report describes an <strong>Intel Core i3-13100 and BIOSTAR H610MHP host</strong>. The owner reported intermittent freezes affecting management access and LXC services. A connected display stopped responding, although the report explicitly says syslog continued producing output. This is more specific than treating the event as entirely log-free. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Original Proxmox forum report"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://forum.proxmox.com/threads/pve-host-freezes-every-2-3-weeks.185009/"> <a href="https://forum.proxmox.com/threads/pve-host-freezes-every-2-3-weeks.185009/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Original Proxmox forum report</a> </span> </p> <p>The owner later reported <strong>improvement after migration</strong>. In an August 3 follow-up, they described moving Docker workloads into Debian virtual machines and stopping the Docker-bearing LXCs. They reported no further freezes at the time of the update, while the video cites a 16-day stable period. Neither statement supplies a controlled reproduction or identifies a particular defective component. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="Owner’s follow-up in the same thread"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://forum.proxmox.com/threads/pve-host-freezes-every-2-3-weeks.185009/"> <a href="https://forum.proxmox.com/threads/pve-host-freezes-every-2-3-weeks.185009/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >Owner’s follow-up in the same thread</a> </span> </p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Observation</th> <th>What it supports</th> <th>What it does not establish</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td><strong>Long initial uptime</strong></td> <td>The earlier workload and software combination operated successfully</td> <td>Reliability after every later update</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Host and services stall</strong></td> <td>The outage extends beyond one application</td> <td>Docker as the root cause</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Migration precedes improvement</strong></td> <td>A useful operational workaround</td> <td>Which changed interaction removed the trigger</td> </tr> <tr> <td><strong>Sixteen stable days</strong></td> <td>A bounded observation period</td> <td>Resolution of every two-to-three-week failure pattern</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <p>The <strong>observation period</strong> deserves scrutiny. Sixteen days falls inside a 14–21 day recurrence window. A longer observation period covering several former failure intervals, comparable workloads, and ordinary maintenance improves confidence, but still falls short of a controlled cause-and-effect demonstration.</p> <p><strong>Operational success and root-cause proof</strong> are separate outcomes. Restoring trusted household services is a valid reason to migrate. Describe the result as improved observed reliability until stronger evidence establishes the mechanism.</p> <h2 id="locate-the-kernel-boundary"> <a href="#locate-the-kernel-boundary" title="Locate the Kernel Boundary">Locate the Kernel Boundary</a> <a href="#locate-the-kernel-boundary" class="h-anchor" aria-hidden="true" title="Locate the Kernel Boundary">#</a> </h2> <div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" style="color:#f8f8f2;background-color:#272822;-moz-tab-size:4;-o-tab-size:4;tab-size:4;-webkit-text-size-adjust:none;"><code class="language-text" data-lang="text"><span style="display:flex;"><span>Docker inside LXC: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Application -> Docker runtime -> LXC namespaces and policy </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -> Proxmox host kernel -> physical hardware </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Docker inside a VM: </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span>Application -> Docker runtime -> guest Linux kernel </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -> virtual hardware / KVM-QEMU </span></span><span style="display:flex;"><span> -> Proxmox host kernel -> physical hardware </span></span></code></pre></div><p><strong>LXC</strong> uses the host kernel. Namespaces, control groups, capabilities, seccomp, and security profiles restrict processes without supplying a separate kernel. Adding Docker inside LXC creates another container-management layer around workloads using the same underlying host kernel. <span itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/WebPage"> <meta itemprop="name" content="LXC architecture and containment features"> <meta itemprop="url" content="https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/introduction/"> <a href="https://linuxcontainers.org/lxc/introduction/" rel="noopener external" target="_blank" >LXC architecture and containment features</a> </span> </p> <p>A <strong>VM</strong> introduces a guest kernel. A guest kernel failure normally affects its VM, while Proxmox continues managing the other guests. The VM still depends on the physical host, hypervisor, storage, and networking.
